-- | An <a>EventSource</a>/<a>EventSink</a> abstraction for an ordered,
--   identified event stream, a checkpoint-by-aggregate log rotation
--   combinator, and a production SQLite backend (WAL,
--   <tt>user_version</tt> schema migrations, async write-behind through a
--   bounded queue, and <tt>VACUUM INTO</tt> archival on rotation).
--   Polymorphic in the base monad via <tt>io-classes</tt> where practical.
@package event-sourcing
@version 0.1.0.0


-- | The types and functions for creating <a>EventSource</a> and
--   <a>EventSink</a> handles, intended to be used as an extension point.
--   
--   A single <a>EventSource</a> and zero or more <a>EventSink</a> handles
--   let an application load and emit an ordered, identified event stream.
--   <a>SQLite</a> is a ready-made implementation.
module Data.EventSource
type EventId = Word64
class HasEventId a
getEventId :: HasEventId a => a -> EventId
newtype EventSource e m
EventSource :: (HasEventId e => ConduitT () e (ResourceT m) ()) -> EventSource e m

-- | Stream all events from the event source.
[sourceEvents] :: EventSource e m -> HasEventId e => ConduitT () e (ResourceT m) ()

-- | Retrieve all events from the event source as a list.
getEvents :: (HasEventId e, MonadUnliftIO m) => EventSource e m -> m [e]
data EventSink e m
EventSink :: (HasEventId e => e -> m ()) -> (HasEventId e => [e] -> m ()) -> EventSink e m

-- | Send a single event to the event sink.
[putEvent] :: EventSink e m -> HasEventId e => e -> m ()

-- | Send a batch of events to the event sink.
[putEvents] :: EventSink e m -> HasEventId e => [e] -> m ()

-- | Create an <a>EventSink</a> from a single-event function, with a
--   default sequential batch implementation.
mkEventSink :: Monad m => (HasEventId e => e -> m ()) -> EventSink e m

-- | Put a list of events to a list of event sinks, batching per sink.
putEventsToSinks :: (Monad m, HasEventId e) => [EventSink e m] -> [e] -> m ()
instance Data.EventSource.HasEventId GHC.Word.Word64


-- | Log rotation for an <a>EventStore</a>: fold the existing events into
--   an aggregate, and once a configured number of events has accumulated,
--   archive them under a log id and start a fresh log from a checkpoint
--   event that captures the aggregate so far.
module Data.EventSource.Rotation

-- | Rotate after this many events have been appended. Must be positive; a
--   value of 0 would trigger a rotation immediately after every
--   checkpoint.
newtype RotationConfig
RotateAfter :: Natural -> RotationConfig
type LogId = EventId

-- | An EventSource and EventSink combined
data EventStore e m
EventStore :: EventSource e m -> EventSink e m -> (LogId -> e -> m ()) -> EventStore e m
[eventSource] :: EventStore e m -> EventSource e m
[eventSink] :: EventStore e m -> EventSink e m

-- | Rotate existing events into a given log id and start a new log from
--   given e.
[rotate] :: EventStore e m -> LogId -> e -> m ()

-- | Creates an event store that rotates according to given config and
--   <tt>StateAggregate</tt>.
newRotatedEventStore :: (HasEventId e, MonadUnliftIO m, MonadTime m, MonadLabelledSTM m) => RotationConfig -> s -> (s -> e -> s) -> (s -> EventId -> UTCTime -> e) -> EventStore e m -> m (EventStore e m)


-- | A SQLite-backed event source and sink.
--   
--   <h2>Architecture</h2>
--   
--   Events are stored in a single <tt>events</tt> table with an integer
--   primary key (<tt>event_id</tt>) and a BLOB column
--   (<tt>event_data</tt>) containing CBOR-encoded event data (via
--   <a>ToCBOR</a> / <a>FromCBOR</a>). The database uses WAL journal mode
--   with <tt>synchronous=NORMAL</tt> to avoid per-write fsyncs while still
--   syncing at WAL checkpoints.
--   
--   <h2>Schema migrations</h2>
--   
--   The schema version is tracked in <tt>PRAGMA user_version</tt> and
--   migrated on open (see <a>applyMigrations</a>). Version 1 stored event
--   data as JSON; opening a version 1 database re-encodes every row to
--   CBOR in one transaction and runs <tt>VACUUM</tt> afterwards to reclaim
--   the freed space. A row that fails to decode aborts the migration (and
--   thereby startup) with <a>EventDecodingException</a>, rolling back to
--   an intact version 1 database. The legacy file-based store (JSON lines)
--   is migrated by decoding each line as JSON and inserting CBOR.
--   
--   <h2>Async write-behind</h2>
--   
--   To keep persistence off the hot path, writes use an async write-behind
--   strategy. <a>putEvent</a> and <a>putEvents</a> encode events eagerly
--   to strict <a>ByteString</a> and enqueue them into a bounded
--   <a>TBQueue</a>. A background writer thread drains the queue and
--   batch-inserts rows using <a>executeMany</a> inside a single
--   transaction, amortising WAL frame writes across multiple events.
--   
--   The last-seen event id <tt>TVar</tt> is updated atomically at enqueue
--   time (not write time), so de-duplication and source-of-truth tracking
--   remain correct even though the physical write is deferred.
--   
--   All SQLite writes go through the single writer thread, preventing
--   concurrent access races. Operations that need data flushed (rotation,
--   reads) use a flush marker: a <a>TMVar</a> is enqueued and the caller
--   blocks until the writer thread has processed all preceding items and
--   signalled it. <a>sourceEvents</a> auto-flushes before reading, so
--   callers always see all enqueued events.
--   
--   <h2>Tradeoffs</h2>
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><b>Writer thread crash surfacing</b>: The background writer is
--   <a>link</a>ed to the calling thread. If it dies (e.g. SQLite I/O
--   error), the exception propagates immediately rather than leaving the
--   caller silently stalled. Use <a>withSQLiteEventStore</a> which handles
--   cleanup (flush + cancel) on exit.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><b>Data loss on hard crash</b>: Events in the queue that have not
--   yet been flushed to SQLite are lost on SIGKILL, OOM, or power loss.
--   This is acceptable when an external source of truth can replay missed
--   events.</li>
--   <li><b>Rotation ordering</b>: <a>rotate</a> flushes the write queue
--   synchronously, archives the current database to
--   <tt>old-state/<a>name</a>-<a>logId</a>.db</tt> via <tt>VACUUM
--   INTO</tt>, then performs DELETE + INSERT. This is safe because
--   rotation is expected to be called only from a single-threaded
--   processing loop, so no concurrent enqueues can occur between the flush
--   and the rotation write. The archive is taken before the DELETE, so a
--   backup failure aborts rotation and leaves the events intact.</li>
--   <li><b>Separate read connection</b>: <a>sourceEvents</a> streams over
--   a dedicated connection. It can run concurrently on other threads, and
--   <tt>VACUUM INTO</tt> fails with "SQL statements in progress" if a
--   streaming statement is open on the same connection as the rotation.
--   WAL mode makes readers on a separate connection safe.</li>
--   </ul>
module Data.EventSource.SQLite

-- | Exception thrown when a persisted event cannot be decoded.
data EventDecodingException
EventDecodingException :: Word64 -> String -> EventDecodingException
[eventId] :: EventDecodingException -> Word64
[decodeError] :: EventDecodingException -> String
data SQLiteLog
MigratingFromFileBased :: FilePath -> SQLiteLog
[legacyFile] :: SQLiteLog -> FilePath
MigrationSkipped :: FilePath -> SQLiteLog
[legacyFile] :: SQLiteLog -> FilePath
MigrationComplete :: FilePath -> SQLiteLog
[legacyFile] :: SQLiteLog -> FilePath

-- | Items in the write-behind queue: either an event to insert or a flush
--   marker that the writer thread signals after processing all preceding
--   items.
--   
--   Events are queued unencoded and CBOR-encoded on the writer thread: the
--   encoding of an event carrying a large payload otherwise sits on the
--   caller's thread. The bounded queue briefly pins event values instead
--   of compact bytes, but the writer drains whole-queue batches so the
--   window is short.
type WriteItem e = Either (TMVar IO ()) (Word64, e)

-- | Bracket-style wrapper around <a>mkSQLiteEventStore</a>. Creates the
--   database, schema, and writer thread, runs the callback, then flushes
--   queued writes and cancels the writer thread on exit. The writer thread
--   is <a>link</a>ed so that crashes surface immediately in the calling
--   thread.
--   
--   If a legacy state file exists at <tt>legacyStateFile</tt>, events are
--   migrated into SQLite automatically before the callback runs.
withSQLiteEventStore :: forall e a. (ToCBOR e, FromCBOR e, FromJSON e, HasEventId e) => Tracer IO SQLiteLog -> FilePath -> FilePath -> (EventStore e IO -> IO a) -> IO a

-- | Create an <a>EventStore</a> backed by a SQLite database at the given
--   file path. The database and schema are created on first use if they do
--   not exist. Returns <tt>(conn, store, flush, reinitLastSeen,
--   cleanup)</tt>. Internal — prefer <a>withSQLiteEventStore</a> which
--   handles cleanup, migration, and flushing automatically.
mkSQLiteEventStore :: forall e. (ToCBOR e, FromCBOR e, FromJSON e, HasEventId e) => FilePath -> IO (Connection, EventStore e IO, IO (), IO (), IO ())

-- | Background writer that drains the queue and batch-inserts into SQLite.
--   Each iteration blocks for at least one item, then flushes everything
--   available. Events are CBOR-encoded here, off the caller's thread, then
--   batch-inserted in a single transaction, and any flush markers in the
--   batch are signalled. Encode errors surface as writer thread crashes,
--   which are <a>link</a>ed to the caller.
writerLoop :: ToCBOR e => Connection -> TBQueue IO (WriteItem e) -> IO ()

-- | Block until all items currently in the write queue have been flushed
--   to SQLite. Sends a flush marker through the queue and waits for the
--   writer thread to signal completion.
flushWriteQueue :: TBQueue IO (WriteItem e) -> IO ()

-- | Migrate events from a legacy newline-delimited JSON file into SQLite.
--   Writes directly to the database, bypassing the async write queue
--   (migration runs at startup before inputs are processed). After
--   inserting, calls <tt>reinitLastSeen</tt> to sync the in-memory event
--   id TVar with the database.
--   
--   Safe to call when the legacy file does not exist (no-op). Not safe to
--   re-run: duplicate event ids will cause a primary key constraint
--   violation.
--   
--   On success the legacy file is renamed to <tt><a>path</a>.migrated</tt>
--   so that subsequent restarts skip the migration step automatically.
migrateFromFileBased :: forall e. (FromJSON e, ToCBOR e, HasEventId e) => Proxy e -> Tracer IO SQLiteLog -> FilePath -> Connection -> IO () -> IO ()

-- | Current schema version. Bump this and add a migration step to
--   <a>migrateStep</a> whenever the schema changes.
nextVersion :: Int

-- | Re-encode a single event row given its event id and stored bytes, used
--   by the version 1 (JSON) to version 2 (CBOR) migration. Must throw when
--   the row cannot be decoded.
type ReencodeRow = Word64 -> ByteString -> IO ByteString

-- | Initialise connection pragmas, then create or migrate the schema to
--   <a>nextVersion</a> using SQLite's built-in <tt>user_version</tt>
--   pragma.
initSchema :: Connection -> ReencodeRow -> IO ()
configurePragmas :: Connection -> IO ()

-- | Read the schema version from <tt>PRAGMA user_version</tt> (0 for a
--   fresh DB).
getSchemaVersion :: Connection -> IO Int
setSchemaVersion :: Connection -> Int -> IO ()

-- | Apply all pending migrations from version <tt>v</tt> up to
--   <a>nextVersion</a>. Each step runs together with its version bump in
--   one transaction (<tt>PRAGMA user_version</tt> is transactional), so a
--   crash or decoding failure mid-migration rolls back to a well-defined
--   version.
applyMigrations :: Connection -> ReencodeRow -> Int -> IO ()

-- | Individual migration steps. Pattern-match on the <i>source</i>
--   version.
migrateStep :: Connection -> ReencodeRow -> Int -> IO ()

-- | Re-encode all event rows using the given <a>ReencodeRow</a> function
--   (the version 1 JSON to version 2 CBOR migration). Rows are processed
--   in batches of ascending event id so memory stays bounded for large
--   databases. Runs inside the caller's transaction.
reencodeAllEvents :: Connection -> ReencodeRow -> IO ()
createEventsTable :: Connection -> IO ()
selectLastEventId :: Connection -> IO [Only Word64]
getEventsASC :: Connection -> IO Statement
insertEvent :: Connection -> (Word64, ByteString) -> IO ()
insertEvents :: Connection -> [(Word64, ByteString)] -> IO ()
deleteAllEvents :: Connection -> IO ()

-- | Archive the current database before rotation removes the events, into
--   an <tt>old-state</tt> subdirectory next to the database, with the log
--   id inserted before the extension (e.g.
--   <tt>old-state/state-42.db</tt>). Uses <tt>VACUUM INTO</tt> so the
--   snapshot reflects all committed (WAL) data in a single self-contained
--   file, regardless of WAL checkpoint state. The destination is removed
--   first if present (e.g. a re-rotation at the same log id), since
--   <tt>VACUUM INTO</tt> requires it not to exist.
backupDatabase :: Connection -> FilePath -> Word64 -> IO ()
instance GHC.Show.Show Data.EventSource.SQLite.EventDecodingException
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Data.EventSource.SQLite.SQLiteLog
instance GHC.Generics.Generic Data.EventSource.SQLite.SQLiteLog
instance GHC.Show.Show Data.EventSource.SQLite.SQLiteLog
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.EventSource.SQLite.SQLiteLog
instance GHC.Exception.Type.Exception Data.EventSource.SQLite.EventDecodingException
